As we heard at last month’s public hearing on March 12, Willets Point Phase II is a transformative project that will bring to New York City its first stadium dedicated to soccer, or should I say football, and create hundreds of units of much-needed affordable housing. This project consists of LUs 30, 31, 32, 33, and 34. Together, these actions will transform Willets Point, which for decades was a hub for auto body shops, into a new neighborhood. This re-

To achieve this proposal, the applicant team, which consists of the New York City Economic Development Corporation in partnership with the Queens Development Group and City Football Stadium Group are seeking five actions. The first action is a text amendment to modify the Special Permit and other needed approvals that currently apply in the Special Willets Point District. This text amendment is needed to reflect the particular aspects of this unique proposal. The second action is a Special Permit pursuant to the amended text to allow the proposed buildings. The third and fourth actions are Special Permits to allow the proposed stadium and hotel uses. The last action is to amend the City’s map to elevate the surrounding street to make the re-envisioned neighborhood more resilient. Council Member Moya has been a champion of this project for many, many years and fully approves this proposal, and I will now like to give the floor to Council Member Moya to give his remarks.
